top10.introHtml: Ranked by condition, reliability, and fun factor for a cheap 4-seat open-air second car. All picks are 4+ seat convertibles. 28 Cars.com listings found (25 extracted); 71 CarGurus (15 extracted from initial load); 38 AutoTrader (21 after seat filter). Two-seat roadsters (Miata, Z3, Boxster, SLK, S2000, TT Roadster, Corvette, etc.) excluded. Only 1 confirmed manual found across all sources (1997 Camaro Z28, AutoTrader); see Manual Tab for likely-manual classics. Image coverage: Cars.com 100%, CarGurus 93%, AutoTrader 86%.

picks.whyGood: Toyota Camry Solara V6 is about as bulletproof as a 4-seat convertible gets. Just 52,505 miles on a 2005 — genuinely low for the age. Local dealer (2 miles from Media) means easy PPI and follow-up. The 3MZ-FE V6 produces brisk pulls without the complication of a turbo. The same car is also listed on AutoTrader (Weathers Motors, $13,779) giving you two price anchors and negotiating room.
picks.whatToVerify: Full top cycle: raise and lower 3x, listen for strut-mount creak. Check rear seat carpet and trunk floor for water staining — Solara rear window seals age and can weep. Inspect strut mounts (common wear at 50k). Confirm V6 timing chain (no belts, but verify oil change history). Light-test all electrics including convertible top motor.
picks.bottomLine: Best value-per-mile in this search and practically in your backyard.

picks.whyGood: The newest, most modern pick in the list: 2017 with GM's 1.6T turbo, heated seats, Bose audio, and a fully automatic power top that works silently. Rated Great Deal and literally in Media — zero commute to PPI. The Cascada is under-appreciated; GM built this one properly and it's genuinely comfortable at highway speeds.
picks.whatToVerify: Top seal condition around windshield header and rear quarters. Confirm top motor and latches work smoothly. 1.6T: check for coolant leaks at throttle body area. Infotainment software version (update available). Front strut boots. Inspect rear differential mount.
picks.bottomLine: Modern, comfortable, local — hardest to argue against for a daily-enjoyable second car.

picks.whyGood: Same platform as #2 at $676 less with 7,500 fewer miles. Also rated Great Deal. Cascadas don't flood the market and hold their condition well. Sewell NJ is an easy 20-mile drive for a PPI. Also appears on AutoTrader at $10,995 giving you a lower price anchor if you negotiate.
picks.whatToVerify: Same as 2017: top seals at header and quarters, top motor/latches, 1.6T cooling system, all latches engage without binding. Confirm interior isn't showing early wear at 71k.
picks.bottomLine: Identical value story to #2 at a lower price — strong buy.

picks.whyGood: Great Deal badge, clean title, no accidents, Toyota reliability. SLE trim means power everything. The 2AZ-FE 4-cylinder is essentially indestructible past 200k with oil changes. At $10,395 you're getting serious Toyota reliability for under $10.5k — hard to find this combination.
picks.whatToVerify: Full top cycle, rear window condition (OEM plastic windows yellow with age — look for aftermarket replacement), rocker panel rust under door sills, PCV hose condition, strut mounts. Note 33mi drive for PPI — worth it.
picks.bottomLine: Best-priced Toyota in the search — get it PPI'd and buy with confidence.

picks.whyGood: Only 42,969 miles on a 4.6L 3V V8 GT — the most fun car in this search by a wide margin. S197 generation Mustang is the classic design loved globally. Great Deal from a franchised Ford dealer adds confidence. The GT V8 is simply irreplaceable at this mileage in budget.
picks.whatToVerify: Top latch at windshield header (common wear spot). S197 spring perch rust — lift the car and inspect thoroughly. Cold-start cam phaser rattle (3V 4.6L known issue — should quiet within 5 seconds). Rear convertible top motor. Exhaust flanges for rust. Note: 40 miles from Media, but worth the drive for this car.
picks.bottomLine: The most fun car in this search — V8 GT with legitimately low miles. Worth the 40-mile drive.

picks.whyGood: S197 platform at $10,459, just 9 miles from Media. The 2012 Cyclone 3.7L V6 makes 305 hp — more than GTs from the 1990s. Under 100k. S197 has massive parts availability and a huge DIY community. Good fun-car choice if you're not committed to the V8.
picks.whatToVerify: Top latch function at windshield header. Spring perch rust (lift and inspect). Water pump seep (known on 2011–13 Cyclone V6). Check rear seat water staining. Confirm convertible top glass is clear (not yellowed). 8.8 axle clunk on launch.
picks.bottomLine: Affordable S197 Mustang practically in the backyard — solid choice.

picks.whyGood: The C70's retractable 3-piece hardtop is the most weatherproof convertible in this list — no fabric to age, no leaking seams. The T5 2.5L turbo five is refined and torquey. Under $10k for a Swedish hardtop convertible is excellent value. Also listed on CarGurus at $10,589 for comparison.
picks.whatToVerify: Full roof cycle is critical — 3-piece hardtop has more hydraulic failure points than a fabric top. Listen for hydraulic pump strain or clunking during the roof cycle. Timing belt service history (due ~100k miles). Check headliner for water staining. Front control arm bushings common wear on C70.
picks.bottomLine: Most unique and upscale pick under $10k — the only retractable hardtop in this search.

picks.whyGood: 70k miles on the N52 naturally-aspirated engine — more reliable than the turbocharged N54/N55. The E93 3-Series is an excellent driver's car: sharp steering, well-sorted chassis, proper drop-top experience. $9,995 is fair for the miles and BMW pedigree.
picks.whatToVerify: PPI mandatory for any BMW: cooling system (water pump, thermostat common failures ~80-100k), VANOS operation, roof hydraulic fluid level and rams condition, rear brakes, valve cover and oil pan for leaks. Get an independent BMW specialist to inspect before buying.
picks.bottomLine: Best driver in this price range — but budget for a thorough PPI and deferred maintenance.

picks.whyGood: Third-gen (F57) MINI Convertible — newest MINI body style with 4 genuine seats and a proper fabric top. 55k miles is impressive for a 2015. Private seller in Easttown (8 miles) is a good sign for single-owner care. Fun to drive, easy to park, strong resale.
picks.whatToVerify: Confirm F57 generation (check VIN). Top fabric condition and header seal. MINI common: water in footwells after rain (test with a hose). B38/B46 engine has improved timing chain vs older N-series but still worth checking. Look for oil leaks at valve cover. Confirm all tech features (CarPlay, navigation) are working.
picks.bottomLine: Fun, close, and well-priced — great pick for a low-drama daily-driver drop-top.

picks.whyGood: The only confirmed manual transmission in this entire search. Z28's LT1 5.7L V8 makes 275 hp and sounds ferocious. 73,590 miles is low for a 1997 — many fourth-gens have 150k+. American muscle at its most honest: loud, analog, rewarding.
picks.whatToVerify: LT1 Opti-Spark ignition module under the distributor (major failure point — ask for recent service or replacement). LT1 distributor base oil leak. Inspect convertible top frame and fabric for rust/rot on a 28-year-old car. Frame rails and rocker sills for rust. Clutch engagement height (should be near floor on a fresh clutch).
picks.bottomLine: Only manual V8 convertible in this search — pure analog fun. Know what you're getting into.

manual10.introHtml: Manual-transmission convertibles in this search are scarce: only 1 confirmed manual (1997 Chevrolet Camaro Z28, AutoTrader) across all three sources this refresh. The remaining picks below are likely manuals based on model/year/trim knowledge — confirm via phone before visiting. Transmission listed as null in source data means it was not reported, not that it's definitely automatic.

picks.whyGood: Only confirmed manual transmission in the full search across all three sources. LT1 5.7L V8, 73k miles, Z28 badge. The definitive driver's pick this refresh.
picks.whatToVerify: Opti-Spark module, LT1 distributor oil leak, top frame rust, frame rails, clutch wear.
picks.bottomLine: Rarest combo this refresh: manual + V8 + convertible. The one.

picks.dealer: Corsinos Service Station and Repair Inc
picks.transmissionNote: Likely manual — 1987 Fox body GT almost always 5-speed; verify in person
picks.whyGood: Fox body Mustang GT 5.0L HO — if it has the T-5 5-speed (extremely common on 1987 GTs), this is affordable classic-muscle fun. Great Deal badge. 16 miles away.
picks.whatToVerify: CONFIRM transmission is manual before visit. EGR delete, oil pan leaks, rear main seal, smog equipment. Top condition on a 38-year-old car.
picks.bottomLine: Classic Fox body 5.0 — confirm the manual first.

picks.transmissionNote: Likely manual — SN95 GT 5.0 commonly 5-speed T-5; verify in person
picks.whyGood: 44,000 miles on a 1994 GT is remarkably low. Private seller typically means single-owner care. 5.0L EFI V8, SN95 platform. If manual, this is the best mileage-to-price manual in the search.
picks.whatToVerify: CONFIRM transmission is manual. Low miles story (highway car? garaged?). Top condition. Cooling system, oil leaks, distributor. Inspect convertible top motor.
picks.bottomLine: Exceptional mileage if the manual story checks out — call first to confirm stick shift.

picks.transmissionNote: Unknown — 1987 Camaro came in both; verify in person
picks.whyGood: Third-gen Camaro Z28 with 57k miles, marked High Demand. Strong V8 classic. Perfection Auto Sales in Vineland carries muscle cars. If manual, excellent find.
picks.whatToVerify: CONFIRM transmission type. Third-gen Camaro common: rear axle bearing, T-tops (if applicable), throttle body injection condition, body rust around windshield and hatch.
picks.bottomLine: Worth a call to confirm manual — third-gen Camaros are increasingly collectible.

picks.transmissionNote: Unknown — fourth-gen Z28 came in both; verify in person
picks.whyGood: Fourth-gen Camaro Z28 just 19 miles away. 119k is high but LT1 engines run reliably past 200k if maintained. At $12,900 the value depends entirely on whether it has the 6-speed Borg-Warner.
picks.whatToVerify: CONFIRM 6-speed manual vs automatic. Opti-Spark ignition condition (same concern as 1997 above). Top frame and fabric condition on a 30-year-old car. Convertible-specific rust at door sills and floor.
picks.bottomLine: Call Wolf's Elite to confirm manual before making the trip.

picks.transmissionNote: Unknown — Trans Am could be 6-speed or 4L60E auto; verify in person
picks.whyGood: 33,887 miles — lowest mileage in the entire manual section and nearly the lowest in the full search. Trans Am GT trim. If it has the T56 6-speed, this is a unicorn.
picks.whatToVerify: CONFIRM manual. At 33k miles this car has been barely driven — ask for full service history. LT1 Opti-Spark likely original. Top condition and frame rust at 35mi away from coast.
picks.bottomLine: Lowest miles in manual section — but at $14,900 the manual confirmation is critical.

mustangs.introHtml: 2005+ Ford Mustang convertibles within the search parameters. The S197 (2005–2014) and S550 (2015–2023) generations represent a clean break from Fox/SN95: stronger chassis, bigger power, better refinement. 4 found this refresh. The 2006 GT is the star pick by a wide margin.

picks.whyGood: Best Mustang in this search — a V8 GT with only 42,969 miles from a franchised Ford dealer carrying a Great Deal badge. The S197 GT's 4.6L 3V V8 is a properly characterful engine. This is the one to beat.
picks.whatToVerify: Cam phaser rattle cold (3V 4.6L known issue — should quiet within seconds). Spring perch rust (lift car and inspect). Top latch at windshield header. Rear convertible motor function. Check for any accident damage at rear quarters.
picks.bottomLine: #1 Mustang pick by a wide margin — V8, low miles, dealer lot.

picks.whyGood: S197 Mustang under $11k, 9 miles away, under 100k miles. The 305hp Cyclone V6 is a capable, efficient engine. Strong entry point for Mustang convertible ownership with great parts support.
picks.whatToVerify: Spring perch rust, water pump weep (known 2011-13 Cyclone), top latch, rear glass clarity, 8.8 axle clunk.
picks.bottomLine: Most accessible Mustang convertible — closest and cheapest S197.

picks.whyGood: S550 generation — the most modern Mustang available: IRS, digital dash, SYNC3. EcoBoost makes 310 hp and gets reasonable MPG. Premium trim means leather, navigation, Shaker audio. High miles but the EcoBoost engine is proven and reliable past 150k.
picks.whatToVerify: Top latch wear at windshield header (common S550 issue). Rear camera. 6R80 auto trans fluid condition. Check rear seat for water staining from top seal. 2.3L EcoBoost: coolant loss check, PCV condition.
picks.bottomLine: Most modern Mustang in this search — worth the miles if it PPI's clean.

picks.whyGood: Newest Mustang in the search (2020), nearly identical platform to the 2018. 132k miles at $14,995 puts it near the top of budget, but you get the most up-to-date S550 features including better SYNC4 infotainment. Langhorne is 33 miles.
picks.whatToVerify: Same S550 checks as 2018. At 132k this is high-mile territory — transmission and top seal inspection are critical. Verify service records.
picks.bottomLine: Newest Mustang available — high miles, so the PPI is non-negotiable at this price.
